## Continuous variable {.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

#### Deterministic part: model formula

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>


$\text{Feeding} = \frac{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{F_\max}}\cdot N}{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{N_\text{\bf half}}}+N}$

$F_\max=\beta_{0}+\beta_{1}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}$

$N_\operatorname{half}$

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
df$N = df$N0
df$Feeding = df$NE
```


```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
formula = bf(Feeding ~ fmax*N/(nhalf+N),
             fmax  ~ scale(HeadWidth),
             nhalf ~ 1,
             nl = TRUE)
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

* Make parameters dependent on predictor(s)
* Use classic `lm`-notation 
* `scale()` the predictor to `mean=0`, `sd=1`    
  can make pars more interpretable:   
  intercept $\beta_{0}=F_\max$ for avg. $\text{HeadWidth}$

:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<br>

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(1701)
p1
```

:::

::::

#### Priors

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>


$F_\max={\boldsymbol{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\beta_{0}}}}+{\boldsymbol{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\beta_{1}}}}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}$

${\boldsymbol{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{{N_\operatorname{half}}}}}$

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
default_prior(formula,

```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

## Continuous variable {.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

#### Priors

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>


$F_\max={\boldsymbol{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\beta_{0}}}}+{\boldsymbol{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\beta_{1}}}}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}$

${\boldsymbol{\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{{N_\operatorname{half}}}}}$

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>


```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
priors = c(
  prior(normal(40,20), nlpar="fmax", coef="Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0 ,10), nlpar="fmax", coef="scaleHeadWidth"),
  prior(normal(30,20), nlpar="nhalf", lb=0)
)
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

* Weakly informative priors for intercept and slope of $F_\max$

:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<br>

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-height: 8

p1
```

## Continuous variable {.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}


```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| output: FALSE
#| fig-height: 8

df$N = df$N0
df$Feeding = df$NE

formula = bf(Feeding ~ fmax*N/(nhalf+N),
             fmax  ~ scale(HeadWidth),
             nhalf ~ 1,
             nl = TRUE)
priors = c(
  prior(normal(40,20), nlpar="fmax", coef="Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0 ,10), nlpar="fmax", coef="scaleHeadWidth"),
  prior(normal(30,20), nlpar="nhalf", lb=0)
)
fit.1 = brm(formula,
            prior = priors,
            family = poisson(link="identity"),
            data = df,
            backend = "cmdstan",
            file = "fit_example_4_1.rds")
```


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
fit.1 = brm(formula,
            prior = priors,
            family = poisson(link="identity"),
            data = df)

summary(fit.1)
```

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
summary(fit.1)
```


:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
plot(conditional_effects(fit.1,
                         effects="N:HeadWidth"),
     points = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(1701)
p = plot(conditional_effects(fit.1,
                             effects="N:HeadWidth",
                             int_conditions = list(N=1:80)),
         points = TRUE,
         point_args = list(alpha=0.5, width=0.5, height=0.5, size=2.5),
         plot = FALSE)
p[[1]] +   
  theme(legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.15, 0.85),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill="lightgray", color="white")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA))
```

* Automatically uses 3 levels for the predictor: $\mu,~~\mu+1\sigma,~~\mu-1\sigma$ 

:::

## Continuous variable {.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}


#### Trends
```{r}
fixef(fit.1)
```
$F_\max$ increases by $\beta_1=10.40$ per $1\sigma$ increase in size

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

scale back to original scale
```{r}
fixef(fit.1)["fmax_scaleHeadWidth", "Estimate"] / sd(df$HeadWidth)
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

or just use `emmeans`
```{r}
library(emmeans)
em_trend = emtrends(fit.1, var="HeadWidth", nlpar="fmax") 
print(em_trend)
```


:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<div style="height: 1.5em;"></div>

```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
#| fig-height: 8
plot(conditional_effects(fit.1,
                         effects="HeadWidth",
                         nlpar="fmax"))
```

## Continuous variable {.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

#### Hypothesis testing

```{r}
hypothesis(fit.1, 
           "fmax_scaleHeadWidth > 0")
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>


Posterior probability:

$P(\beta_1>0)=1.00$

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

::: {style="background-color:  var(--highlight-high-bg); border-left: 4px solid var(--highlight-high-border); padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 0 8px 8px 0;"}
<span style="font-size: 1.0em;">
**→ Yes, feeding rates are positively affected by predator size.**
</span>
:::


:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<div style="height: 1.5em;"></div>

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
p = plot(
  hypothesis(fit.1,
             "fmax_scaleHeadWidth > 0"),
  plot = FALSE
)
p[[1]] + geom_vline(xintercept=0)
```

<div style="height: 1.5em;"></div>

## Continuous variable with link{.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

#### Deterministic part: positive parameters

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

$\text{Feeding} = \frac{\textcolor{black}{{F_\max}}\cdot N}{\textcolor{black}{{N_\text{half}}}+N}$

$$
\begin{align}
F_\max&=\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{\exp}}\left( \beta_{0}+\beta_{1}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}\right)\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{\ >0}}\\
\Leftrightarrow \textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{\log}}\left( F_\max\right)& =\beta_{0}+\beta_{1}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}
\end{align}
$$


<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
df$N = df$N0
df$Feeding = df$NE
```


```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
formula = bf(Feeding ~ fmax*N/(nhalf+N),
             nlf(fmax ~ exp(fmaxlog)),   # exp(b0+b1*x)
             fmaxlog ~ scale(HeadWidth), # b0+b1*x
             nhalf ~ 1,
             nl = TRUE)
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

* Define new parameter `fmaxlog` with its linear model
* Transform to `fmax~exp(fmaxlog)`

:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<br>

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(1701)
p1
```

:::

::::


## Continuous variable with link{.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

#### Priors



$$
\begin{align}
F_\max&=\exp\left( \beta_{0}+\beta_{1}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}\right)\\
\Leftrightarrow \log\left( F_\max\right)& =\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{\beta_{0}}}+\textcolor{var(--highlight-high-border)}{\boldsymbol{\beta_{1}}}\cdot\text{HeadWidth}
\end{align}
$$

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>


```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
priors = c(
  prior(normal(log(40),1), nlpar="fmaxlog", coef="Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0,1),       nlpar="fmaxlog", coef="scaleHeadWidth"),
  prior(normal(30,20), nlpar="nhalf", lb=0)
)
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

* Priors for intercept and slope of `fmaxlog`,    
  which is on logscale

:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<br>

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(1701)
p1
```

:::

## Continuous variable with link{.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}


#### Trends
```{r}
library(emmeans)
em_trend = emtrends(fit.2, var="HeadWidth", nlpar="fmaxlog") 
print(em_trend)
```

<div style="height: 32px;"></div>

* $\log(F_\max)$ increases by $+0.27$ per $1$ unit of size (*additive*)

* $F_\max$ increases by $\times\exp(0.27)=1.31$ per $1$ unit of size (*multiplicative*)

* That's $31\%$ increase per $1$ unit of size

:::

::: {.column width="05%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

<div style="height: 1.5em;"></div>

```{r}
#| eval: TRUE
#| fig-height: 8
plot(conditional_effects(fit.2,
                         effects="HeadWidth",
                         nlpar="fmax"))
```

:::

## Continuous variable {.smaller}

#### Summary

* Put a linear model `par ~ varA` inside your nonlinear model
* Test effects with `hypothesis()` 
* `scale(varA)` can ease prior specification   
  back-transform slopes with `emtrends()`
* Parameter bounds cannot be guaranteed via priors
* Define linear models on unrestricted scale, manually transform to restricted scale
* log-link for $0<\text{par}$: `parlog~varA, nlf(par~exp(parlog)`   
* logit-link for $0<\text{par}<1$: `parlogit~varA, nlf(par~1/(1+exp(-parlogit))`


## ... and more! {.smaller}

<br>

* Mix factorial and numerical treatments variables   
  `par ~ factorA + varB`  
  `par ~ factorA * varB`  
* Random effects     
  `par ~ (1|group)`  
* Parameter itself has nonlinear relationship with other variable?   
  Use a GAM!   
  `par ~ s(var)`
* Prediction model too complex to just write in `bf(y~...)` ?    
  Write separate `Stan`-function which is used in `brms` !    
  `brm(..., stanvars = )`
